subject.title: Execution anti-drift guards: artifact-gated status, escalation timers, and no-idle-after-green

question: Should OpenClaw add enforceable anti-drift guards for agent status/progress loops, and if so should they be narrow diagnostics-driven runtime behavior or a new feature-flagged enforcement surface?
rationale: The requested behavior is broader than a narrow bug fix because it changes runtime progress semantics, adds persisted guard state, and proposes a new flag/telemetry surface; automation cannot safely choose that product boundary.

options.title: Scope into existing diagnostics
options.body: Implement only a narrow embedded-run/session diagnostics guard that reuses current progress and stuck-session state, avoiding a broad new feature flag unless later evidence requires it.

options.title: Adopt the full enforcement surface
options.body: Add persisted per-run guard state, artifact-gated status rules, escalation timers, telemetry, and an explicit rollout flag after maintainer design approval.

options.title: Defer pending live repro
options.body: Keep the current partial guards and require a concrete transcript or live reproduction before designing new runtime enforcement.

recommendation.title: Scope into existing diagnostics
recommendation.body: Implement only a narrow embedded-run/session diagnostics guard that reuses current progress and stuck-session state, avoiding a broad new feature flag unless later evidence requires it.

likelyOwner.reason: Current central runtime guard history points most strongly to Peter Steinberger, and the decision is about the same embedded-run/session diagnostics owner boundary.
